text:
Full-catalog diagnostics and benchmark HR@10 measure different quantities: sampled ranking can reverse model comparisons, so retain the pinned 99-negative evaluator for selection and treat full-catalog effects as explanatory evidence ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Proposed efficient implementation: encode each original/perturbed history once, stream catalog scores in chunks, and accumulate exact target rank as 1 + count(score > target_score) + count(score = target_score and item_id < target_id). This avoids sorting and storing all catalog scores. Explicit tie rules matter because [PyTorch topk](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.topk.html) does not guarantee stable tied indices.

For paired perturbations, freeze eligibility from the original history; recomputing exclusions after deletion/shuffling confounds representation effects with candidate changes. Exclude padding, count each candidate ID once, and explicitly define repeated-target handling: retain the target exactly once for target-ranking probes, flag repeated targets, and report repeat/nonrepeat strata. Keep simulator unseen-item recommendations under their separate eligibility rule. These are proposed diagnostic controls, not established findings from the searched literature. Validate chunked ranks against exhaustive sorting on small examples, including ties, repeats, padding and chunk boundaries.

Estimate uncertainty by resampling users with replacement within category, preserving every paired observation for each sampled user, then recomputing category means and their four-category macro-average; use seeded 95% intervals. This follows the dependence-preserving principle of the [cluster bootstrap](https://journal.r-project.org/articles/RJ-2023-015/). To establish predictive usefulness, preregister diagnostic directions and model interventions, then test whether baseline diagnostic effects predict subsequent validation HR@10 gains across independent trials. Check out-of-sample prediction, category consistency and paired gain intervals; exploratory correlation alone is insufficient. Keep hidden test outcomes untouched and report GPU cost alongside diagnostic coverage.
